name: text striping reducer
claim: At equal output chars the striping reducer (stripe-1.0) keeps more rare (df-1) units and more identifier units than the head-and-tail `ends` reducer on a repo corpus; the 2x rare bar, the 1.5x number bar and any live benefit are recorded apart as not-supported (wvxbnl).

models.result: 43 repo blobs, 516 runs, 0 failures. Auto at 0.25 (n >= 2000), stripe over ends: rare 43% vs 27% (1.57x), ident 87% vs 33% (2.62x), num 47% vs 31% (1.49x). At 0.1: rare 1.21x, ident 3.18x, num 0.95x. Common (top-decile) units 38% vs 85%. Lines mode: rare 0.96x at 0.25. Supported: more rare and ident units at 0.25 and 0.5; not supported at 0.1 for num.

name: text striping reducer, refuted halves
claim: Refuted half of the striping reducer concept (tzhwkd, rqmtzo): at least 2x rare and 1.5x number units over head and tail, and a cheap model answering with fewer drill-ins; both missed or not shown.

models.result: Rare 1.57x at auto 0.25, under the 2x bar (over the 1.2x refutation line); num 1.49x, under 1.5x; 0.95x at 0.1. The S12 spec fixture is synthetic and tuned feasible, so it does not stand for these ratios.

Live probe, 36 requests, 6 blobs per condition, one run per cell, no marker legend: no benefit over head and tail. Fact asks correct full 6/6, stripe 1/6, ends 1/6; about keyword score 0.73, 0.37, 0.57; prompt tokens 1930, 792, 532. Drill-in counts not measured; n is tiny, so this is no proof either way.

name: striped skeleton notation
claim: The skeleton notation (header line, kept spans, [~N,wW,lL,kX] markers, `[~` escaped as `[~~`) parses back to the exact source offsets with verify true on every blob of a repo corpus; the marker-overhead bar is recorded apart as not-supported (ysgpcu).

models.result: Parse-back true on 43 of 43 blobs in all 12 mode and fraction groups (516 runs, 0 failures); determinism by double run, key-order permutation and fingerprint 43/43; idempotent 43/43; header class equals classify() on every reduced row.

name: striped skeleton notation, marker overhead
claim: Refuted half of the notation concept (lxpgsj, jhdkfa): marker and header overhead under 30% of the output on blobs over 2000 chars; measured above that bar.

models.result: Median marker overhead auto 43% at 0.1, 36% at 0.25, 21% at 0.5; under 30% on 43 of 126 rows (auto, n >= 2000); chars mode 63% and 54% at 0.1 and 0.25.
Without a legend the skeleton was read as corrupted or garbled text on the docs blob; effect of a legend not tried.

fault: Given a skeleton with no marker legend: on the json blob answered 500 for 401 and on the code blob 1500 for 12000 (both answers were in view, number guessed); on the log blob answered that the text does not contain the commit (answer was in view), a refusal not a guess; on the docs blob called the skeleton corrupted or garbled.
handled: Probe frames were identical across conditions on purpose, so no legend was given and nothing was handled. A frame that explains the markers was not tried.
evidence: docs/concepts/results/stripe-probe-2026-11-21.jsonl (cells json, code, log, docs; stripe condition)

fault: The S16 known check is weak: it fails only when `after < K.length` is false, so it passes if a single one of the identifiers kept without known is not kept again. It does not test that the term is kept less often in aggregate (R18).
handled: Not fixed here (scripts/test-stripe.mjs is the seams agent's); seams tightens the condition in the next iteration.
